section.title: Cool Down Activity
section.para: The height in feet, \(h\), of a stomp rocket (propelled by a short blast of air) above the ground after \(t\) seconds is given by the equation \(h(t)=5+100t-16t^2\). Here is a graph that represents \(h\).

image.alt: Graph of the quadratic function h(t)=5+100t−16t2 on a coordinate plane, origin O . Horizontal axis scale 0 to 7 by 1’s, labeled “time (seconds)”. Vertical axis scale 0 to 200 by 50’s, labeled “height above ground (feet)”. Some of the points are (0 comma 5), (1 comma 89), (2 comma 141), (3 comma 161) to a maximum near (3 point 125 comma 161 point 25), then decreasing through (4 comma 149), (5 comma 105), (6 comma 29) and (6.3 comma 0).

div.para: The graph intersects the vertical axis at 5.

list.item: How does the 5 in the equation relate to the graph?

div.para: It indicates that the initial velocity of the rocket was 100 feet per second upward.

list.item: What does \(100t\) in the equation mean in terms of the rocket?

div.para: This indicates the effect of gravity pulling the rocket back toward Earth.

list.item: What does the \(-16t^2\) mean in terms of the rocket?
About when does the rocket hit the ground?
